title: Anchors taken from a 'likely' record (schools, people, handles, domains, company legal-name aliases) still confirm other records
evidence: Temp test through stepDeepCheck: Google given; record 1 (likely) yields school Stanford, origin weak:<id>; namesake 'charged with fraud' record graded confirmed, reasons 'names Google','names Stanford University'. Separately, alias {Zeta Holdings Inc, origin weak:x1} confirmed 'Jane Roe, director of Zeta Holdings Inc, was charged'.
scenario: Given company is a large employer (Google) or the name is a mononym. A likely record adds a Stanford school anchor (weak:). A namesake's fraud charge naming Google and Stanford is upgraded to confirmed by regrade() and becomes a red flag. A legal name learned by companyFacts from a likely record (weak:) also confirms any record naming it. This breaks the written rule that a likely record never confirms other records.
fix: In anchorNeeds, set a flag whenever any anchor in schools/people/handles/domains/aliases has a non-strong origin, not only companies. In gradeOf, when the grade is confirmed and that flag is set, grade again with viewOf keeping only strong-origin anchors of every kind (filter aliases by origin too). Cap at likely unless that strict grade still confirms. Add the two cases above as tests.
verifyNote: Reproduced via stepDeepCheck: 'Jane Roe of Google' graded likely added school Stanford (origin weak:id); a namesake 'charged with fraud' record naming Google and Stanford was graded confirmed. anchorNeeds flags only weak companies; matchSubject counts any school/person/handle/domain as the second fact. Breaks FOUNDER-CHECK rule 1.
betterFix: In anchorNeeds, flag any non-strong anchor of every kind, aliases included. On a confirmed grade, regrade with viewOf keeping only strong anchors. orgMatcher reads aliases from the original subject through a closure, so viewOf alone cannot hide weak aliases: pass the filtered alias map through (subject.anchors in the view) or give matchSubject a strongOnly option. Add both regression tests.

title: Start runs the first step with no lease: a retried start or a reload during it runs every seed lookup twice
evidence: Temp route test: a start with a slow source, then a second start after 50 ms, then a step on the jobId it returned. The second start returned resumed:true with the same jobId. The source log shows subject:Jane Roe and company:Acme Corp each asked twice; the step got 409.
scenario: The client wraps startJob in patiently(), so a network drop or a 5xx during the 40 s start sends the start again. A reload during the start also finds the running job through GET ?name. The new request resumes the job and steps it, and leaseJob succeeds because start never took a lease. All seed lookups go to the paced hosts twice. The start also ignores saveNext's false result and returns progress that was never saved.
fix: After createJob, call leaseJob(id, { owner }) before stepping, or insert the row with a lease in its state. Release the lease in a finally block, as the step path does. Have the resume branch answer the running job without stepping. When saveNext returns false on start, answer with the saved job's progress (getJob) rather than the unsaved one.
verifyNote: Start steps with no lease. A start retried by patiently(), or a reload (latestJob), gets the running job back. The client then steps it, and leaseJob succeeds while the first start is still stepping, so seed lookups run twice. The resume branch does not step itself (that part of the report is wrong), and saveNext's false is ignored.
betterFix: Take the lease inside the create, or call leaseJob right after createJob. Release it in finally. Leave the resume answer without a step. When saveNext returns false, answer with getJob's progress.

title: Starting again with new optional details silently resumes the old running check and drops them
evidence: In the same temp test, the second start added otherNames ['Jane Smith'] and website 'acmecorp.io'. It came back resumed:true with the first jobId, and nothing reported that the new details were not used.
scenario: An investor starts 'Jane Roe / Acme Corp', sees namesakes, and within the hour runs it again (the fresh 'Run again' path) adding a profile URL, other names, a website or a confirmed network company. findLatestJob matches on name and company only, so the old check comes back. The details meant to separate her from namesakes are dropped with no message.
fix: Resume only when the stored inputs match: compare state.given, otherNames and assumedCompany with the new validated input, or a hash of them saved on the job. When they differ, start a new job (or stop the old one with stopCollecting) and tell the page.
verifyNote: If the investor re-submits the same name and company with new details while the old check is running (new runKey, so fresh), startJob reaches the server. findLatestJob matches only name and company with status running, so the old job comes back with resumed:true and the new details are dropped without a word. Once the old check is done, a new one starts normally.
betterFix: Save a hash of the validated inputs (given, otherNames, confirmedCompany or useNetworkCompany) on the job and resume only when it matches. Otherwise stop the old job (stopCollecting) and create a new one, and tell the page that the earlier run was replaced.

title: Earlier companies the user types get no court, enforcement, insolvency or watchlist screens
evidence: tieOf({why:'an earlier company given'}) returned 'affiliate'. With sanctions-lists, court-dockets, doj-press-releases, us-enforcement-actions and uk-companies-house as connectors, only uk-companies-house was asked about the typed earlier company 'Zeta Labs'.
scenario: An investor types a founder's earlier venture under 'Earlier companies'. EARLIER_COMPANY_GIVEN does not match PRIMARY_TIE, and the seed passes no venture flag. The company is planned as a plain affiliate: SEC company, Companies House, the French register, YC and the joint web searches only. A DOJ case, an SEC action, a bankruptcy or a sanctions listing against that company is never looked up, and the report does not say so.
fix: Seed typed earlier companies with venture: true (pass origin { anchor: 'given', venture: true }), so isScreenTask and planTasks run the SCREEN_SOURCES on them. Or treat 'an earlier company given' as primary in tieOf. Either way, list them in coverage as screened.
verifyNote: Reproduced: with otherCompanies ['Zeta Labs'], Zeta Labs went only to uk-companies-house and the web-search joint templates. Sanctions, court dockets, DOJ and enforcement were never asked about it, while the given company was. tieOf('an earlier company given') returns 'affiliate' and the seed passes no venture flag.
betterFix: Seed typed earlier companies with origin { anchor: 'given', venture: !isLargeEmployer(c) }, so their screens run but a typed large former employer (Google) does not fill the report with that company's litigation. Show them in coverage as screened, or as checked only for ties when they are not screened.

title: The second reader's statedRole is stored but never shown or used; the header's promise of 'the role shown is the one the sentence states' is not met
scenario: verifyGaps sets statedRole. noteThread copies it. report.js threads map only {kind,value,why,relation,suggested}, and networkLink companiesOf reads why, so the role is lost. That is harmless now, but a later engineer may wire it up while it is still wrong (see the first finding: 'founder' for Ford).
fix: Fix the stretch logic first (first finding). Then either surface statedRole in report.threads and the network 'other' group, or remove it.
evidence: grep statedRole across src: written in gaps.js and deepCheck.js:811 only, never read.
verifyNote: Nothing reads statedRole; report.js:1199 drops it. It is also wrong on a true link. 'Trevor Milton founded Nikola in 2014 and later backed Romeo Power' gives Romeo Power the role 'founder', because statedRole takes the first ROLE_WORDS match anywhere in the stretch.
betterFix: Remove statedRole for now. If it is kept, compute it only from the link word that governs the target (the one the first fix selects), never from the whole stretch.

title: publicReport does not strip ifRightPerson entries, so gradeText, score and matchFixed reach the page despite finding.js saying deep.js strips them
scenario: report.js line 903 builds ifRightPerson entries as {...lead, ...}, a full finding that includes gradeText (up to 1,500 characters of cleaned grading text, often more than the 700-character quote). publicReport maps redFlags, companyMatters, possibleNamesake, sections and claimChanges through strip, but not ifRightPerson. The text has been cleaned, but it is an internal field the page was promised never to see.
fix: Add ifRightPerson: (report.ifRightPerson || []).map(strip) in publicReport, and add a test that walks the public report and asserts that no gradeText, score, via or matchFixed key appears at any depth.
verifyNote: Read the code: report.js line 911 pushes {...lead} entries (including gradeText, score and via) into ifRightPerson. publicReport at deep.js line 215 never maps ifRightPerson through strip, so the internal fields reach DeepCheck.js. The text is already privacy-cleaned, so the severity is low.
betterFix: Add ifRightPerson: (report.ifRightPerson || []).map(strip). Better still, strip generically: walk every array of findings in the report, nested 'more' entries included. Add a test asserting that no gradeText, score, via or matchFixed key appears at any depth.

title: The sanctions screen timed out on its first load and stayed "answered only in part" for the whole check
scenario: Live run (cold cache): "sanctions-lists failed (timeout): Timed out after 16s"; the list download finishes in the background, but the lookup is never asked again, so the most important screen reads partial.
fix: A watchlist, court or regulator screen that failed on a timeout or a 5xx is put back once and run again in a later round (the list is cached by then); only a second failure is final.

title: A check takes about ten minutes locally (420 lookups, 9 rounds), up from about five before the new sources
scenario: Eric Glyman / Ramp r10: 615 s. Bluesky, Mastodon, Stack Overflow, writing feeds and the web archive account for most of the tail.
fix: Look at eval/founder/runs/r10/glyman.log for where the time goes; cap low-value presence lookups per check (a handful, not 15 to 18 each), run them only after the screens and the profile sources, and stop them first when the budget runs low. Do not cut screens.
